finding: There is no live range for this job yet, so this is a first build. Built totals, labor only (no parts), stated hours x $120-$160/hr (the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2015 Nissan Sentra about $35-$80 (0.29-0.5 hr); midsize 2016 Nissan Rogue about $43-$80 (0.36-0.5 hr); truck 2017 Nissan Titan about $60-$106 (0.5-0.66 hr); luxury 2015 BMW 328i about $35-$80 (0.29-0.5 hr). Across classes that is roughly $35-$106. How this compares: the car figures bracket the two priced benchmarks, RepairPal's $49-$72 and the Kelley Blue Book average of $60-$72 quoted second-hand, so the build is about right for a paid rotation on a car; the truck top of $106 is above RepairPal's $49-$72 for a Silverado 1500 and should be read as a ceiling. Candidly, this is a menu-price service and the menu price often sits below a book-time build: many shops charge a flat fee near the bottom of this range, fold the rotation into an oil change, or do it free. Rotation is commonly free for the life of the tires where the tires were bought (Discount Tire, Costco, Les Schwab, Firestone, Sam's Club and others), so $0 is a normal price and a driver should check that first. A shown range of about $0-$100, with a typical paid price of $35-$80, would be honest. How solid the labor times are: weak. No maker-printed time for a plain maintenance rotation was found for any conventional example vehicle. The low ends are Tesla service-manual flat rate times (0.29 hr Model 3, 0.36 hr Model Y) and the truck high is Tesla's 0.66 hr for a Cybertruck; none is the example vehicle. The 0.5 hr figure is Nissan's all-models warranty time for swapping all four wheels and resetting the tire pressure system during a pull diagnosis, the nearest stated operation and a little more than a bare rotation. The luxury high is a tire chain's general 'about 30 minutes', not a book time. Not found: a posted paid rotation price from a chain (the Walmart and Les Schwab pages reached list none) and a Honda, GM, Hyundai/Kia, Subaru or FCA bulletin printing a 'rotate tires' time. Cars with different tire sizes front and rear, or directional tires, cannot be rotated the usual way.
extras: A quote may add: wheel balancing (often sold with the rotation as 'rotate and balance'); a tire pressure sensor reset or relearn; including a full-size spare in the pattern; removing and refitting wheel locks or hubcaps; extra labor for dual rear wheels, oversized or heavy off-road tires; remounting tires on the wheels where sizes differ front to rear or tires are directional (a larger job); a brake inspection or a wheel alignment recommended from the tire wear found; shop supplies and sales tax. Before paying, check whether the rotation is free where the tires were bought or included with an oil change or a maintenance plan.
